transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-26
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Sofia Moreno (HaloEdge Head of ML); Ben Carter (HaloEdge Infra Lead); Rina Sakamoto (HaloEdge Security); Amir Khalid (HaloEdge PM)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be fuzzy)
- Kickoff to align pilot and implementation runway.
- Discussed VPC/private options, KMS integration, and runbook items.
- Action items captured; agreed to POC benchmark week in January.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Reyes: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, happy holidays to those who are out, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm joined by Priya and Liam on our side. Can everyone do a quick intro?
00:08 Sofia Moreno: Hi I'm Sofia, Head of ML at HaloEdge. We're building customer-facing doc summarization and search features, want to move from a dev sandbox to production.
00:14 Ben Carter: Ben, infra lead. I'm responsible for network, VPCs, access, all that.
00:18 Rina Sakamoto: Rina from security, I'll be owning compliance questions and SSO integration.
00:21 Amir Khalid: Amir, PM, I'll coordinate stakeholders and timelines.
00:25 Priya Nair: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — align on scope for pilot, confirm security and network constraints, and agree next steps for the POC.

05:12 Liam O'Connor: So from an SE perspective we typically recommend running an initial warm-up on Redwood Hosted API to validate prompts and quality, then move to Dedicated or Private depending on latency and data residency. But given your compliance notes, I'm guessing Private (VPC) is top of mind?
05:27 Sofia Moreno: Yeah we have customers who require data never leave our VPC, so private deployment is preferred. However cost/latency tradeoffs are a concern — we want to understand the lift.
05:40 Jordan Reyes: Totally, that's expected. Private gives you full control over network egress and KMS integration but there is an ops overhead. We can propose a hybrid: pilot on Dedicated in a private VPC peered to your account, and if all good move to on-prem or customer-managed private.
05:56 Ben Carter: When you say "peered to our account" is that a VPC peering or do we need a transit gateway? We have strict firewall egress rules.
06:08 Liam O'Connor: We typically do VPC peering for initial POCs — it's simpler. For larger deployments we support Transit Gateway. We'll include network diagrams in the runbook. (note: some transcript wording may be off here)
06:22 Rina Sakamoto: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys/HSM? We need CMEK for sensitive PII transcripts.
06:30 Jordan Reyes: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS via standard KMS integrations, and for Dedicated we have options to integrate with your KMS — there is an additional configuration step. We'll include that in the security pack.

12:03 Amir Khalid: Timeline — we want a two-week POC where we validate latency and throughput, then decide on a 3-month pilot. Is that realistic?
12:16 Priya Nair: Yes, two weeks for benchmarks is reasonable. We'll own orchestration for the bench runs on our side with SE support. We suggest a baseline phase and a stress phase.
12:29 Sofia Moreno: Success metrics: p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, throughput 50 QPS sustained, and cost per 1M tokens under our target. Also quality regression <5% on our eval prompts.
12:46 Liam O'Connor: Noted. We'll provide a benchmark sheet — it's a simple Google sheet with fields for sample prompts, tokenization, and measurement hooks.

18:10 Ben Carter: Access — for staging should I open an IAM user or use temporary roles? We prefer short-lived roles.
18:20 Liam O'Connor: Short-lived roles (assume role) are preferred. We'll provide a small terraform snippet for the minimal policy.
18:30 Ben Carter: Okay we'll aim to provide that by next week.

22:50 Rina Sakamoto: A couple security items: audit logs retention (we need 1 year), SAML/SSO for SSO login, RBAC mapping to our org groups. Are these supported in Redwood Console?
23:05 Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and RBAC. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM; retention is a config in Private. We'll share the exact retention mechanics in the security pack.
23:20 Rina Sakamoto: Also, do you have SOC 2 / ISO compliance documentation?
23:28 Jordan Reyes: We do. I'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper to the meeting notes. There may be a bit of automated transcription noise on that doc name though.

29:00 Sofia Moreno: On the model side — we'll start with an open model from your catalog, right? We want a model that's quantized single-GPU friendly; some of our shorter prompts are sensitive to quantization noise.
29:18 Liam O'Connor: We can recommend specific model variants — for production we often recommend medium-size quantized models for better throughput. We'll include model recommendations and quantization tradeoffs. Also note that the runtime has KV cache and prefix caching, which can reduce per-token cost significantly if your use case has repeated context.
29:38 Sofia Moreno: When you say KV cache, do you mean the key-value cache for autoregressive decoding? We have a lot of long conversation contexts.
29:46 Liam O'Connor: Yeah that's right — small mis-transcript: I said key-value "cash" earlier in the doc but it's cache. It helps with repeated tokens and multi-turn sessions.

35:05 Amir Khalid: Anything we should prepare on the product side?
35:12 Priya Nair: Sample dataset (5k-20k tokens worth), a representative eval set, and a list of prompts/edge cases. Also contact for NetOps and Security.
35:22 Sofia Moreno: We'll prepare a 2000 sample doc set and an eval of ~200 prompts.
35:28 Ben Carter: I'll get staging IAM and VPC peering details.

42:10 Jordan Reyes: Logistics for POC week — we propose Jan 12 initial baseline run, Jan 13-14 stress and latency tuning, Jan 15 quality evaluation and cost estimates. We'll send a calendar hold after this call.
42:28 Priya Nair: I'll set up weekly sync cadence for the POC and invite both NetOps and Security to the first sync.

49:00 Rina Sakamoto: A few smaller items — encryption at rest, data residency in EU (some customers), and data retention. We need to confirm where logs live in Dedicated mode.
49:14 Liam O'Connor: In Dedicated and Private modes you can choose region and we can set retention. Logs can be forwarded to your S3 or your SIEM. We'll include exact flows in the runbook.

54:01 Jordan Reyes: Quick recap: Redwood to share onboarding runbook, security pack (SOC2, KMS integration guide, SAML guide), pricing worksheet; SE to share benchmark template and terraform snippet for role; HaloEdge to share sample dataset, provide staging IAM and answer security questionnaire. POC week Jan 12-16 tentative. Any final q's?
54:25 Sofia Moreno: Sounds good. Thanks, Jordan.
54:30 Ben Carter: thanks.
54:33 Priya Nair: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links.
54:36 Meeting closed.
